script.name: How to Write SEO Blog Posts with AI: The 6-Phase Workflow
script.description: A complete process for using AI tools to research, outline, draft, optimize, and humanize SEO blog content that ranks in search engines.

tool.name: AI writing assistant (ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini)
SEO keyword research tool (Ahrefs or Semrush)
Semantic SEO tool (Clearscope or Surfer SEO)

step.name: Phase 1 — Keyword and Intent Mapping
step.text: Read the top five SERP results for your target keyword. Identify the dominant content format, primary angle, and gaps. Extract People Also Ask questions. Write a one-page intent brief capturing search intent type, content format, gaps, PAA questions, and reader's end goal. Load this brief into every subsequent prompt.

step.name: Phase 2 — Build the Prompt Stack
step.text: Use a four-prompt sequence: an outline prompt loaded with your intent brief, a section-drafting prompt run once per H2, an E-E-A-T injection prompt for key sections, and a transition prompt. Never generate a full article in one prompt — section-by-section drafting allows explicit depth control.

step.name: Phase 3 — Skeleton-First Draft Generation
step.text: Generate the outline first. Read it critically as a reader would — check logical sequence, argument flow, and redundancy between H2s. Fix structure before drafting. Then generate body sections one at a time, loading section-specific context (data, examples, quotes) into each prompt before generating.

step.name: Phase 4 — The Human Layer
step.text: Inject five elements AI cannot generate: a real-world example with a verifiable outcome, original or cited data with your interpretation, a dissenting opinion, a specific qualified tool opinion with a boundary condition, and a first-person observation paragraph. Use the Human Layer Checklist before advancing.

step.name: Phase 5 — On-Page SEO Pass
step.text: Run a structured on-page checklist: title tag, meta description, H1, first-100-words keyword placement, H2/H3 structure, image alt text, internal links, schema markup, URL slug, and word-count-vs-intent match. Then run the draft through Clearscope or Surfer to identify missing semantic terms.

step.name: Phase 6 — Post-Publish Audit
step.text: At 30, 60, and 90 days post-publish, run a Google Search Console diagnostic. Use the three-column framework: GSC signal → what it means → action. High impressions/low CTR means rewrite title and meta. Low impressions/poor position means check indexing and strengthen internal links. Impressions rising/position stuck means build topical cluster links.

mainEntity.name: Can AI-written content actually rank on Google?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — AI-written content ranks on Google regularly. The ranking standard is quality and helpfulness, not authorship method. Content that demonstrates genuine expertise, addresses real search intent, and provides information users can't easily find elsewhere will rank, regardless of whether a human or an AI wrote the first draft.

Google does not issue penalties for AI-written content as a category. The manual action Google applies is for spammy automatically generated content — content produced at scale specifically to manipulate rankings without editorial oversight or genuine value. AI-assisted content with human review and genuine helpfulness does not meet that standard.

mainEntity.name: How do I add E-E-A-T to AI content?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add E-E-A-T through five specific injections: a real-world example with a verifiable outcome, original or cited data with your interpretation of its implication, a documented failure or acknowledged limit, a specific tool opinion with a boundary condition, and a first-person observation paragraph. These cannot be generated by AI because they require actual experience.

mainEntity.name: What prompts should I use for SEO blog articles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use a four-prompt sequence: an outline prompt loaded with your intent brief, a section-drafting prompt run once per H2, an E-E-A-T injection prompt for two or three key sections, and a transition prompt that connects sections. Load your intent brief into every prompt to maintain topical coherence.

mainEntity.name: How long should an AI blog post be to rank?

acceptedAnswer.text: Match the content length of the top five ranking pages for your target keyword. For informational queries, this is typically 1,500 to 3,500 words. For commercial comparison queries, often 800 to 1,500 words. Padding to hit a word count target dilutes topical density and works against quality signals.
